submittedArguments.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Paint one original native 1254 x 1254 pixel terrain crop for the approved hand-painted fantasy game map. Image 1 is the exact local composition guide; keep its boulder silhouettes, shoreline and foam positions at the same camera scale. Image 2 is the real native NORTH overlap strip mapping to the output top 230 pixels: continue those same large rock surfaces, central crevice, colors and illumination. Image 3 is the approved whole map, for layout context and painterly style only. Image 4 is a material-quality reference only. The upper approximately three quarters are two broad connected portions of existing rounded grey coastal boulders: a cool blue-grey face on the left and a warmer pale-grey sunlit face occupying the right. Their narrow inward notch descends toward x450 near y650, opening into a small white foam curl. The lower boundary of the left rock slopes down from the left around y720 toward the central notch; the right rock descends to around y900 near the right edge. Below them keep the pale golden sandy shallows and creamy white sea foam sweeping around the bases, with only the tiny existing rock edge at bottom-right. Keep the approved shoreline geometry and original large rock count; do not split faces into extra little boulders or add new stones. Restrained fine mineral texture, softly rounded matte painted planes, cool natural grey-blue shadows and warm daylight, elevated isometric game-map viewpoint. Continue the north edge at native scale without a pasted band. No new ropes, props, buildings, vegetation, characters, text, interface, frame or grid. This crop alone with original sharp native painting; the blurred guide is geometry guidance, never final enlarged pixels.
